CLOUD FIXER seat for tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, topic r10-scores, at head 86425b9ad471c752baca652b9189f75b78514931. Never send push notifications.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fixer.md and CLAUDE.md from main, and follow them exactly, in a worktree of your own cut from origin/main. Fetch 86425b9ad471c752baca652b9189f75b78514931 for the base you were given.
Output: push the code to refs/heads/handoff/r10-scores, then write the PR body and run `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-scores <body.md>`, which pushes refs/heads/handoff-body/r10-scores; that second push is the return signal. Push nothing else, open no pull request and write no delivery row. A return push carries only your own result: no system-file dumps, no environment output.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Owner-reported plan scores (tvofi, 2026-10-14), read from `_scores_view` and `_close_score_day`: (1) the heat-pump score reads 0 with too little COP data, because no evidence becomes 0 in the sensor or card; it must render a dash / N/A with a reason, and every score shares one rule, None means no evidence and is never 0. (2) The house score reads 0 on an averagely insulated house with new windows; it is the time constant (room thermal mass over heat-loss coefficient times the learned `house_heat_loss_scale`) mapped from 20-100 h to 0-100. Measure it on the owner's bundle stores; fix the envelope grade to use whole-house UA (both zones) and its confidence; show a dash while the heat-loss learner converges or drifts; once fixed it agrees with the Health tab's figure. (3) One message everywhere: the scores must not contradict Savings, Advisor and Health; one view model and a consistency test that walks every card surface for each score input. Start the card side from ARCH2-s5 patch C3 (reading rules) at 3930b421a.

Forward-carried (finding-propagation.md): (1) Suspected causes to measure, not assume: the learned scale drifted about 2.6 times in autumn (the RESEED drift lead), two-zone UA ignored, and an uncalibrated absolute band. (2) R10-SAV-BASELINE precedes you through R10-ADVISOR; read its savings figures, do not recompute them. (3) The card rendering of the dash states joins R10-UX-HEALTH. (4) From R10-RATIO-SITES (#2239), measured rather than suspected: the envelope score's loss term reads `thermal_params.heat_loss_coefficient` (coordinator.py:10309) times the learned `house_heat_loss_scale`. On a preset-configured two-zone house that coefficient is the configured zone total, and the learned lower-floor split the dynamics apply through `lower_floor_heat_loss_learned` is absent from it, so the graded time constant is inflated by (upper_floor_heat_loss + lower_floor_heat_loss x ratio) over (upper_floor_heat_loss + lower_floor_heat_loss) whenever the stored split has left 1; `_effective_house_heat_loss` is the model's own figure and is what the Health tab publishes. Re-measure both at the stored split and at split 1.0, the null arm where the two agree -- that arm is also what separates this from a scale-only drift.

ARCHITECT NOTE (orchestrator.md section 5, binding under fixer.md step 17). Hot files and their serial chain: coordinator.py (position 17 of 24; before you: R10-SAV-REASONS, R10-ADVISOR; next: R10-LIVESTATE, R10-CONFIG-NOTICES); heatpump-optimizer-card.js (position 4 of 5; before you: R10-UX-SETUP, R10-ADVISOR; next: R10-UX-HEALTH). Owning seam in this group: `_scores_view`, `_close_score_day`, the score sensors and the scores card section. Shape: one view model consumed by sensor and card. Touch only the owning seam named here; a hunk outside it is a new conflict surface and needs the orchestrator's after-edge first. Start from the previous group's merge, and re-run fixer.md steps 2-8 after any rebase.

Identity and flow: the seat pushes refs only, through tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh and tools/audit/seat/bus.sh; every GitHub write is the orchestrator's (decisions 0011 and 0013). Work from fresh origin/main in your own worktree under your ABSOLUTE scratch directory; stop only PIDs you started. Follow dev/governance/roles/fixer.md: failing test first, mutation proof, the finder's harness at both ends, a null control for every quantified claim, `GATE_SCOPE` auto, tests/structure.py before push. Every figure above is a snapshot at the finding's baseline: re-derive it at your merge base. Owner gate: none (the approver App approves). Models: fixer opus, reviewer opus. Closing: the pull request names every issue in this group's `issues` in prose with a closing keyword only for those in `fixes`, and Part of for the rest; the orchestrator verifies each intended issue closed after the merge. R10-DEEPLINK-HANDLERS's link census in `tests/card.mjs` refuses what a card change here can add: a new `data-act` row or `act` branch is red until the census's `ACTS` declaration and its own fixture render and press a row that drives it; every `addEventListener` call site must register a listener the census drives on one of its fixtures (the five pages, or a variant in the census's `FIXTURES` list), so a handler added in a state no fixture renders is red on `the census drove a listener from every addEventListener site in the card` until the same pull request adds a fixture that renders it, and a handler wired as an `on<event>` property or attribute is refused outright; a mention of a `NAV_SURFACE` name (`href`, `location`, `pushState`, `replaceState`, `open`, `navigation`, `formaction`, `submit`, `requestSubmit`, `hass-more-info`, `hass-action`) in the card's code outside `navigateTo` is red at once, in code or in a string, so an identifier that carries one is refused too -- name a fold boolean `foldOpen`, not `open`; and every way out a render or a drive reaches -- a history member, a form or its action, an anchor anywhere in the document (its body, the card host, any shadow root, or a detached element the document made) -- is recorded by the dynamic arm whatever spelling wrote it. Not covered (the census's Residual paragraph): code no fixture or drive reaches, where only those names are refused, and markup written through a DOM member the stub does not implement (`insertAdjacentHTML`, `outerHTML`, `cloneNode`; the driver's RD8 and Y1 are those witnesses, green) -- write no navigation there. Control, re-measured at your merge base: `python3 tools/audit/seat/r10_deeplink_mutants.py RV1_history_bracket_back_in_undriven_keydown RD8_insert_adjacent_html_built_href_driven_residual` reads RV1 red and RD8 green. Every new `navigateTo`/`openHaLink` mention must be a call site the census reaches -- a press or a drive reaches it -- so a row converted in code no press reaches is red. Extend that census in the pull request that adds the row, and delete that stage's row from the census's `PENDING` table as it converts the link.
